Wren 2.5.2 is a pure performance release: nothing looks different, it just does less work every time the numbers move. No new features and no behavior changes — if you are happy with 2.5.1, this one is simply a little lighter.

## Highlights

- **Idle tabs stop working.** Only the tab you are looking at stays in the view hierarchy now. Previously every tab stayed subscribed to the session and redrew on each sample even while hidden, so switching tabs and leaving them open cost more than it should have. Hidden tabs now cost nothing.
- **The app ledger builds only what you can see.** The process list in Apps is built lazily, so a long ledger no longer constructs — and re-sorts — rows that are scrolled off screen on every update.
- **Your per-tab choices survive a tab switch.** Sort order, the search text, and the pinned wiki entry moved out of the views and into the router. With tabs no longer kept alive, this is what keeps "sort by memory" still sorted when you come back.

## Changed

- The selected tab alone is kept in the view hierarchy; hidden tabs are no longer subscribed to the session or holding onto their view trees for the life of the window.
- Apps ledger rows are created lazily, so update cost scales with what is on screen rather than with the length of the list.
- Per-tab view state (Apps and Advanced sort order, Wiki search text and pin) lives on the router so it persists across tab switches.
- The wiki remembers the last "What is this?" it acted on, so revisiting the tab does not replay an old request over your own browsing.

## Install

Download `Wren-2.5.2-macOS-arm64.dmg`, open it, and drag Wren to Applications. Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon.

## First launch (Gatekeeper)

Wren is ad-hoc signed rather than notarized with a paid Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper will say the developer "cannot be verified". Control-click the app, choose **Open**, then **Open** again (or System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Open Anyway**).
